name: Santa Monica
tagline: Beach city with the Expo line, a walkable downtown and some of the Westside's priciest streets.

name: Venice
tagline: The canals, the boardwalk and Abbot Kinney: bungalows and modern boxes a few blocks from the sand.

name: Marina del Rey
tagline: Condo towers and townhomes around the harbor, between Venice and the airport.

name: Playa Vista and Playa del Rey
tagline: A planned tech-campus district beside the Ballona wetlands, and the quiet beach town below the bluffs.

name: Culver City
tagline: Studio town with a revived downtown, the Expo line and a mix of bungalows and new apartments.

name: Mar Vista
tagline: Hilly grid of post-war houses and new builds between Venice and Culver City.

name: Westchester
tagline: Family streets on the bluffs above the airport, next to Loyola Marymount.

name: Palms
tagline: Dense, central and relatively affordable for the Westside: apartments and small houses along the Expo line.

name: West Los Angeles
tagline: Sawtelle's Japantown, Rancho Park and the Expo line stops between the 405 and Westwood.

name: Westwood
tagline: UCLA's neighborhood: the Wilshire condo corridor, Westwood Village and single-family streets to the north.

name: Brentwood
tagline: Leafy Westside enclave of large lots north of Wilshire, from San Vicente up into the canyons.

name: Bel Air
tagline: Gated estates and canyon homes in the hills between Beverly Hills and Brentwood.

name: Century City
tagline: High-rise condos beside the office towers and the Westfield mall, on the old Fox backlot.

name: Beverly Hills
tagline: The flats, the hills and Rodeo Drive, with its own school district and city services.

name: West Hollywood
tagline: Dense, walkable city between Hollywood and Beverly Hills: the Sunset Strip, the design district, condos and 1920s courtyard apartments.

name: Beverly Grove and Fairfax
tagline: Between the Grove and Cedars-Sinai: duplexes, Spanish bungalows and new apartments.

name: Hollywood Hills West
tagline: Laurel Canyon and the hills above the Sunset Strip: houses on winding streets with city views.

name: Sherman Oaks
tagline: Valley neighborhood of ranch houses and hillside homes along Ventura Boulevard.

name: Studio City
tagline: Ventura Boulevard's restaurant row, hillside streets south of the boulevard and the studios across the river.

name: Encino
tagline: Ranch houses and estate lots along the base of the Santa Monica Mountains, next to the Sepulveda Basin.

name: Tarzana
tagline: Big lots south of the boulevard and 1950s tracts north of it, named after the Burroughs ranch.

name: Woodland Hills
tagline: West Valley suburb with Warner Center's towers and leafy streets climbing toward Mulholland.

name: Calabasas
tagline: Gated communities and a small old town just over the city line, with its own school district.

name: Northridge
tagline: Cal State Northridge, 1960s ranch tracts and the Fashion Center in the north-west Valley.

name: Granada Hills
tagline: North Valley suburb of mid-century houses, with larger lots up toward the hills.

name: Porter Ranch
tagline: Newer master-planned tracts on the north Valley slopes, built mostly since the 1990s.

name: Chatsworth
tagline: Horse properties and ranch houses under the sandstone peaks of the west Valley.

name: North Hollywood
tagline: The NoHo Arts District, the end of the Metro B line and dense blocks of apartments and small houses.

name: Van Nuys
tagline: Mid-Valley neighborhood of modest post-war houses, apartment blocks and the G line busway.

name: Burbank
tagline: Media city with its own schools, airport and utility; tidy mid-century streets up to the Verdugo foothills.

name: Glendale
tagline: Third-largest city in the county: hillside neighborhoods, the Brand Boulevard core and dense condo blocks.

name: La Cañada Flintridge
tagline: Foothill city known for its school district and large lots under the Angeles National Forest.

name: La Crescenta
tagline: Foothill community of sloping streets and mid-century houses between La Cañada and Tujunga.

name: Sunland-Tujunga
tagline: Rural-feeling foothill neighborhoods at the top of the Valley, backing onto the national forest.

name: Manhattan Beach
tagline: Small beach town with the Strand, top-rated schools and a tight housing stock.

name: Hermosa Beach
tagline: Smallest of the beach cities: the Strand, Pier Avenue and tightly packed lots.

name: Redondo Beach
tagline: The harbor, the pier and the Riviera on the south side; townhome-heavy North Redondo near the 405.

name: El Segundo
tagline: Small town behind the aerospace campuses: bungalows, a Main Street and its own schools.

name: Torrance
tagline: Big South Bay suburb with the Del Amo mall, Old Torrance and well-regarded schools.

name: Palos Verdes Peninsula
tagline: Ocean-view lots, horse trails and the Peninsula school district, with slow-moving land on the south side.

name: Hawthorne
tagline: Home of the SpaceX campus, with modest post-war houses and some of the South Bay's lowest prices.

name: Gardena
tagline: South Bay city with a deep Japanese-American history and small houses on standard lots.

name: Carson
tagline: 1960s tracts, Cal State Dominguez Hills and the Dignity Health Sports Park at the edge of the harbor.
